name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.exists_pureState_nonzero_on_star_mul_self
title: A pure state detects a nonzero square

content.display_title: A pure state detects a nonzero square
content.one_sentence_role: Detects a nonzero element through its positive square without an algebra separability assumption.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra, and let $a\in A$ be nonzero. There is a pure state $\varphi$ on $A$ such that $$\varphi(a^*a)\ne0.$$ Here a state is a continuous complex-linear functional positive on positive elements and satisfying $\varphi(1)=1$; pure means extreme in the real convex state space.
content.assumptions: No separability assumption is made on $A$. The element detected in the conclusion is $a^*a$, rather than an assertion about $\varphi(a)$.
content.conclusion: One functional $\varphi$ is simultaneously a state, pure, and nonzero on $a^*a$.
content.proof_summary: Choose a nonzero spectral value of the positive square, realize it as a character value on its generated commutative algebra, and extend that character to a pure state.
proof_steps: Put $b=a^*a$. The $C^*$-identity gives $\|b\|=\|a\|^2>0$, so $b\ne0$. It is self-adjoint. Its spectral radius equals $\|b\|$, and compactness of its spectrum supplies $z\in\sigma(b)$ with $|z|=\|b\|>0$.

Let $D=C^*(1,b)\subseteq A$, the norm-closed unital $*$-subalgebra generated by $b$. Since $b$ is self-adjoint, $D$ is commutative. The character-space identification with $\sigma(b)$ gives a character $\chi$ of $D$ with $\chi(b)=z\ne0$. These are the two applications in [Spectral radius and the generated-algebra character map](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/Faithful.lean#L27-L64): self-adjointness supplies the norm-radius equality, and the chosen spectral point is an input to the surjective character map.

Apply [Pure-state extension of a character](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/State/Extension.lean#L231-L258) to this closed commutative unital $D$ and this character $\chi$. It produces a state $\varphi$ on $A$ which is pure and satisfies $\varphi(x)=\chi(x)$ for every $x\in D$. Substituting the same $b=a^*a\in D$ gives $$\varphi(a^*a)=\varphi(b)=\chi(b)=z\ne0.$$ The first two outputs of the extension theorem give the remaining state and purity conditions.
